items.explanation: Attackers use rules like this to hide payment emails, so the real vendor's replies never reach you while they redirect the money.
A copy of every email goes to an outside account, which lets someone read your invoices and conversations and time a fake payment request.
This deletes payment emails before you see them, a common way to hide a vendor's warning that their bank details were changed.
Your CEO's emails are copied to an outside Gmail account, which lets an attacker study how your CEO writes and then impersonate them.
An outside address is approved to receive your mail, which is how attackers keep reading a mailbox after a password reset.
